title: Referral revenue with OR across two tables
prompt: Referral dashboard: about 15 calls per second, about 900 ms each. Plan: full scans of Customers and of
IX_Orders_CustomerID or PK_Orders, a hash join, and the OR applied as a residual filter after the join. There is no
index on Customers.ReferredByCustomerID. A typical customer has referred 0 to 50 customers. 312 customers are
self-referrals (ReferredByCustomerID = CustomerID) from an old signup bug that cannot be cleaned yet. Payouts are
computed from these numbers, so they must not change.
data_notes: Azure SQL Database, General Purpose Gen5, 8 vCores, compatibility level 160. READ_COMMITTED_SNAPSHOT ON. Query Store READ_WRITE. Collation SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS. All foreign keys are trusted. Statistics: auto create and auto update ON; a nightly job updates Orders, OrderLines and Payments with FULLSCAN.

Orders: 30M rows, 2016 to now, ~12k per day now. The 25 partner customers own ~9M orders (30%), up to 1.2M each. Other customers average ~10 orders (max ~400). The density estimate for CustomerID is ~15 rows. Status: Shipped 83.8%, Cancelled 7%, Paid 6%, Returned 3%, Pending 0.2% (~60k rows, all from the last 72 hours). SalesChannel: Web 62%, Store 20%, Partner 12%, Phone 6%. PromoCode is NULL for 85%. ShipRegionID is NULL for Store pickups (~20%). OrderDate is datetime2(7); Partner and Store imports stamp one timestamp on a whole batch, so many orders of one customer share an OrderDate.

Customers: 2.0M rows. Tier S = 1.85M, G = ~150k, P = 25 partner accounts (CustomerID 1 to 25). IsActive = 1 for 88%. Email is NULL for ~9% (~180k rows, ~160k of them active). About 2% of non-NULL emails are shared by two or more customer rows (households). ReferredByCustomerID is non-NULL for 18%; 312 rows are self-referrals (ReferredByCustomerID = CustomerID, CustomerID 500001 to 500312). AccountNumber always matches 'AC' + 10 digits (CHECK constraint).
baseline_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS OrderCount, SUM(o.TotalAmount) AS Revenue
JOIN qe.Customers c ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID

correct_families.description: Two seekable branches combined with UNION on the order key, which removes exactly the orders that satisfy both branches.
reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS OrderCount, SUM(x.TotalAmount) AS Revenue
JOIN qe.Orders o ON o.CustomerID = c.CustomerID

correct_families.description: Filter Orders by the set of customers: the customer and the customers it referred. IN ignores duplicates in the set.
reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS OrderCount, SUM(o.TotalAmount) AS Revenue
SELECT c.CustomerID FROM qe.Customers c WHERE c.ReferredByCustomerID = @CustomerID);

correct_families.description: UNION ALL with the first branch's rows excluded from the second. It is exact only because CustomerID is NOT NULL.
reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS OrderCount, SUM(x.TotalAmount) AS Revenue
JOIN qe.Orders o ON o.CustomerID = c.CustomerID

traps.why: A self-referral customer's own orders satisfy both branches. UNION ALL counts them twice.
traps.told_apart_by: Parameter case self_referral: one of the 312 customers that referred themselves.
example_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS OrderCount, SUM(x.TotalAmount) AS Revenue
JOIN qe.Orders o ON o.CustomerID = c.CustomerID

traps.why: UNION on TotalAmount alone merges different orders that have the same amount.
traps.told_apart_by: Two orders of the customer with the same TotalAmount.
example_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS OrderCount, SUM(x.TotalAmount) AS Revenue
JOIN qe.Orders o ON o.CustomerID = c.CustomerID

min_improvement.basis: Full scans of Customers and an Orders index become a few hundred seeks.

key.reference_notes: The first branch can drop the Customers join because Orders.CustomerID is NOT NULL with a trusted foreign key.
